rows.grounds: relative pronoun referring to previously mentioned feminine plural entities
verb expressing the effect of that knowledge

items.question: What effect does mere discriminative knowledge have upon great dangers?
premises: Discriminative knowledge is the means indicated in the preceding context.
Mere knowledge alone can act as an effective cause.
Great dangers are subject to removal by this knowledge.
items.inference: Therefore, by the mere knowledge of that discrimination, great dangers flee.
uncertainties: The feminine plural antecedent of yāsāṃ is not explicitly named in this verse and depends on prior context.
items.plain_english: By the mere knowledge of which, great dangers flee away.
